purpose: L7 functional replay of the OpenSSH consumer family at the exact b78 frozen candidate. The b78 freeze records l7_replay as NOT_RUN (court/freeze-b78/FREEZE-b78.json, safe_compatible.l7_replay); this file is the evidence that the replay was subsequently run, and the identity every measurement was taken at.
repository_head_note: HEAD moves only by committing evidence (AGENTS.md section 22); this measurement is bound to the source/artefact identity below, not to HEAD.

sshd_session_tree_binary.note: unstripped link-tree copy; never executed by sshd

sshd_session_executed.note: the path compiled into sshd (SSHD_SESSION); this is the session binary that served every login. Stripped install copy; same build as sshd_session_tree_binary by install provenance, not proven byte-equivalent.

linkage.sshd_session_executed: readlink /proc/<pid>/exe = install/libexec/sshd-session; /proc/<pid>/maps resolves libcrypto.so.3 from /work/artifacts/phase2/install/lib; 0 libssl mappings
linkage.sftp_server_executed: links libc only (linux-vdso, libc, ld-linux); no libcrypto and no libssl at all

venue.container: openssl-rs-court (image openssl-rs-court:1), up before this batch
venue.caps: memory=8g memory-reservation=8g memory-swap=8g (swap pinned equal to memory, so no growth by swap), pids=2048, cpus=8, oom-score-adj=500; per-exec RLIMIT_DATA=4 GiB

cgroup_at_start.memory_events: oom=1 oom_kill=1 (pre-existing, from an earlier session; zero events added by this batch)

venue.memory_deviation: AGENTS.md section 6.1 caps a command at min(8g, available-16g) with a 2g floor; with available=13-14 GiB that floor is NOT met, so no compilation, build, clippy or cargo test was run in this batch. Only prebuilt consumer binaries were executed, largest process sshd/sshd-session at well under 100 MiB RSS, under the court's existing 8g/8g cap which cannot be recomputed without destroying the running container. A build in this session would have been refused.
venue.heavy_commands: one at a time: keyformat (2 s), probe (about 60 s), supplement (about 25 s); docker ps and /proc/pressure/io checked first
venue.residual_process: one zombie remains: sshd-session pid 57389, State Z, PPid 1. It was SIGKILLed after the supplement's held-open login but the container's PID 1 (sleep infinity) never reaps children, so it will persist until the container is recreated. It holds no memory, no file descriptor and no listening socket; the probe port was closed and re-bound successfully in a later run.

WORK default moved to court/freeze-b78/l7/work; PORT 2222 -> 2242 to avoid colliding with a Phase-17 run

everything else, including every case, argument and Phase-17-era case label, is unchanged

The authority-writes/candidate-reads half of keyformat_probe.sh therefore cannot run.

partial_substitute.detail: Section C reads OpenSSH's own shipped regress private keys (rsa_openssh.prv, ed25519_openssh.prv), produced by upstream OpenSSH, not by this candidate: both read OK. ecdsa256_openssh.prv is not present in the 9.9p1 regress tree, so the ECDSA case is absent rather than failing.
partial_substitute.limit: a static shipped artefact is not a live authority ssh-keygen; it is weaker evidence than the Phase-17 cross-reader differential

w2_live_sshd_and_login.reproducibility: the probe was run twice (first run with a probe-addition that was then removed); all 18 negotiated tuples were identical across both runs
w2_live_sshd_and_login.comparison_with_phase17: the two cases the Phase-17 script labelled 'EXPECT FAIL: key parse defect' (ECDSA and RSA host-key parsing) both PASS at b78. The Phase-17 defect is not reproduced at this candidate. This is recorded as a compatibility difference, not as a fixed assertion: the labels are inherited text and were left unchanged in the copy.

w3_concurrency.config: sshd MaxStartups 64:30:100 (raised from the 10:30:100 default, exactly as Phase 17 did, so the 16 simultaneous unauthenticated starts are not randomly dropped); each client 30 s timeout, ConnectTimeout=10, publickey only

results.executed_session_witness: live sshd-session pid observed in /proc; exe -> server-b78/install/libexec/sshd-session; libcrypto resolved from artifacts/phase2/install/lib; 0 libssl mappings
results.sftp_transfer: sftp put + ls + get over the candidate ssh/sshd/session path: byte-identical round-trip

w4_sftp_server_and_session_identity.note: sftp-server does not link libcrypto or libssl at all (ldd shows only libc, ld-linux and vdso). Its L7 pass therefore exercises the sftp protocol path through the candidate ssh/sshd and the candidate crypto used by them, but says nothing directly about the candidate library via sftp-server itself.

transcripts.raw_workdir: court/freeze-b78/l7/work (per-case ssh -v logs, generated keys, sshd logs; 572 KiB total)

does_not_prove: Single host, self-connection: client and server are the same b78 build on loopback. A failure could not be localised to one side, and agreement between them is not evidence of interoperability with any other implementation.
No third-party peer: no OpenSSH upstream, BoringSSL, OpenSSL-native, rustls or commercial SSH client/server was used. Only algorithms this build offers were negotiated.

Functional evidence only (AGENTS.md section 8): no ASan/valgrind/Miri run, no adversarial or fuzzing court (section 13 deep-state court not run), no constant-time or timing measurement (section 11 dudect not run), no Wycheproof/ACVP vectors in this batch.

Authentication policy is deliberately permissive for the probe (PermitRootLogin yes, StrictModes no, root login with pubkey, dedicated privsep user created inside the disposable container). This exercises the crypto path, not a hardened production baseline.
Concurrency is 16 simultaneous loopback logins, not sustained load, and not a stress or rekey-under-load workload.
L7 functional PASS is not SAFE_COMPATIBLE graduation (AGENTS.md section 7): it says nothing about the safety obligations of the mechanisms these binaries reach.

The executed session binary is the stripped install copy (ee5f4ef6...), not the link-tree binary (f5ad1a23...). Its provenance is the same install; byte-equivalence between the two is not proven here.
The matrix is not exhaustive: it covers the algorithms the Phase-17 probe names plus the b78 default negotiation, not every kex/cipher/MAC/host-key combination the build advertises.
The ssh-keygen key-format differential against an authority ssh-keygen was NOT_RUN, so cross-implementation key-file compatibility is not established by this batch.
residuals: No authority-linked OpenSSH build exists in this venue, so keyformat_probe.sh sections A(reader)/B are NOT_RUN and section C runs candidate-only. A venue with an authority ssh-keygen is required to close this.

Host swap was 28-29 GiB of 31 GiB used with 11-14 GiB available throughout. Section 6.1's build cap floor could not be met, so this batch contains no compilation at all; any future L7 batch that needs a rebuild must wait for host memory or run in a lower-capacity court.
court/ is listed in .gitignore (/court/), so these scripts and transcripts are invisible to git status and must be added with `git add -f` if the orchestrator wants them tracked.
The executed sshd-session and sftp-server are the stripped install copies; the evidence binds the executed digests and the tree digests separately rather than asserting they are the same bytes.

OpenSSH 9.9p1 does not include finite-field DH in its default kex list; the sshd config re-enables group14/16/18 and gex explicitly (as Phase 17 did). That is a deliberate configuration, so these cases do not represent default 9.9p1 negotiation.

The Phase-17 'EXPECT FAIL' labels for ECDSA/RSA host keys are now stale: both pass at b78. The labels are left verbatim in the copy to keep the case set byte-identical, and the actual result is recorded here.
scope_statement: This file records observed L7 functional behaviour of the b78 OpenSSH consumer binaries on one host against themselves. It does not certify memory safety, cryptographic assurance, interoperability, or SAFE_COMPATIBLE graduation.
